stories.title: Tether posts $1.5 billion operating profit in Q2 as reserve buffer halves
stories.summary: Tether reported $1.5 billion in operating profit for the second quarter, even as its excess reserve buffer fell by roughly half. The stablecoin issuer's results underscore its continued profitability from holding low-risk assets against USDT issuance.
stories.whyItMatters: Tether's reserve cushion is a key indicator of how well the largest stablecoin is collateralized, and a shrinking buffer draws more scrutiny even amid strong headline profits.
whatToWatch: Whether Tether publishes further detail on what drove the reserve decline
Future attestations showing whether the buffer stabilizes or keeps shrinking
questions: What specifically caused the buffer to fall by half in one quarter?
Does a smaller buffer change risk assessments of USDT's peg stability?

stories.title: Coinbase posts $359M loss despite years spent diversifying beyond bitcoin
stories.summary: Coinbase reported a $359 million loss for the quarter, a result that comes after roughly five years of efforts to build revenue streams beyond core bitcoin trading. The report highlights how exposure to broader crypto market swings still weighs heavily on the exchange's results.
stories.whyItMatters: Coinbase is a bellwether for the health of the US crypto industry, and a large loss despite diversification efforts raises questions about how resilient exchange business models really are.
whatToWatch: Coinbase's next earnings call for management commentary on the loss
Any strategic shifts in product mix following this result
questions: Which specific business lines drove the loss?
Is this a one-off or a sign of a structural profitability problem?

stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs close July in the green despite late-month selloff
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs finished July with net positive flows overall, even though the last part of the month saw notable selling pressure. The monthly result suggests underlying demand held up despite short-term volatility.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows remain one of the clearest proxies for institutional appetite for bitcoin, so a positive month despite a late selloff is a signal worth tracking for sentiment shifts.
whatToWatch: August flow data to see if the late-July selling trend continues or reverses
Whether large redemptions cluster around specific funds
questions: What drove the late-month selling — macro news, profit-taking, or something fund-specific?

stories.title: How an attack drained $70 million from bitcoin cold wallets without touching the devices
stories.summary: A reported $70 million in bitcoin was lost from cold wallets through an attack that reportedly never physically compromised the hardware devices themselves, pointing to a vulnerability elsewhere in the security chain — likely in software, supply chain, or user process rather than the device hardware.
stories.whyItMatters: Cold storage is widely marketed as the gold standard for securing crypto; an exploit that bypasses the device itself challenges assumptions many holders rely on for security.
whatToWatch: Technical post-mortems detailing the exact attack vector
Vendor responses and any firmware or process fixes
questions: What was the actual point of compromise if not the device?
Are other hardware wallet users still exposed?

sources.title: How bitcoin cold wallets lost $70 million in an attack that never touched the devices

stories.title: Coldcard exploit, now at $38 million and growing, dents confidence in self-custody
stories.summary: A vulnerability tied to the Coldcard hardware wallet has led to at least $38 million in losses so far, with the figure still climbing. The incident is prompting discussion about whether some investors will shift from self-custody toward custodial options like ETFs.
stories.whyItMatters: Self-custody is central to crypto's value proposition, so a high-profile hardware wallet exploit could push retail and institutional users toward regulated, custodial alternatives.
whatToWatch: Whether the loss total continues to rise as more victims come forward
Any shift in ETF or exchange custody inflows following the incident
questions: How many users remain vulnerable if they haven't updated or migrated funds?
Will Coldcard's response restore confidence or accelerate the shift to custodial products?

stories.title: Coinbase's weak quarter splits Wall Street on timing of recovery
stories.summary: Coinbase's disappointing second-quarter results have divided analysts, with some debating whether the company's growth prospects beyond core crypto trading justify optimism, while others remain cautious about near-term recovery timing.
stories.whyItMatters: Analyst disagreement over Coinbase's trajectory reflects broader uncertainty about how quickly crypto-native companies can diversify revenue away from volatile trading fees.
whatToWatch: Analyst rating and price target changes following the earnings miss
Coinbase guidance on non-trading revenue growth
questions: What specific catalysts would resolve the analyst split?
How much of the miss is cyclical versus structural?

stories.title: Circle secures New York trust charter as stablecoin regulation advances
stories.summary: Circle has obtained a New York trust charter for a subsidiary, a move that comes as regulatory frameworks for stablecoins continue to take shape in the US. The charter gives Circle a more formal regulatory footing in one of the country's key financial jurisdictions.
stories.whyItMatters: Regulatory approvals like this help legitimize major stablecoin issuers and could set a template other issuers follow as US stablecoin oversight solidifies.
whatToWatch: How the trust charter affects Circle's operations or product offerings in New York
Whether other stablecoin issuers pursue similar charters
questions: Does this charter meaningfully change Circle's compliance obligations or just formalize existing practice?

stories.title: New York sues Kalshi, alleging illegal gambling operation, seeks $36 billion
stories.summary: New York has filed suit against prediction market platform Kalshi, alleging it is running an illegal gambling operation rather than a legitimate trading venue, and is seeking $36 billion in damages. The suit adds to ongoing legal and regulatory friction between prediction markets and state gambling regulators.
stories.whyItMatters: The case could set precedent for how prediction markets are classified and regulated across states, with implications for other platforms operating in similar legal gray areas.
whatToWatch: Kalshi's legal response and any motions to dismiss
Whether other states follow New York's lead with similar action
questions: Will federal regulators' prior stance on Kalshi's CFTC status conflict with New York's gambling claim?
How realistic is the $36 billion damages figure?

stories.title: Tether's Q2 profit boosted by US Treasury holdings
stories.summary: Tether reported $1.5 billion in second-quarter earnings, with US Treasury holdings cited as a key driver of the profit. The results reflect the stablecoin issuer's continued reliance on short-term government debt as its primary yield-generating reserve asset.
stories.whyItMatters: Tether's profitability is closely tied to interest rates on its Treasury holdings, meaning its earnings could shift significantly if rates move or its reserve composition changes.
whatToWatch: Future rate decisions and their effect on Tether's reserve income
Any changes in Tether's reserve asset composition
questions: How exposed is Tether's profit model to a falling-rate environment?

stories.title: Coldcard-linked bitcoin losses grow to $70 million, Galaxy Research finds
stories.summary: Galaxy Research estimates that losses tied to the Coldcard hardware wallet vulnerability have climbed to $70 million, up from earlier lower estimates. The growing figure suggests the exploit's scope was larger than initially understood.
stories.whyItMatters: An independent research estimate raising the loss total signals the incident may be more severe than early reports indicated, which matters for anyone assessing hardware wallet risk.
whatToWatch: Further updates to the loss estimate as more data comes in
Whether Galaxy or other researchers identify additional affected wallets
questions: How was the $70 million figure calculated, and could it rise further?

stories.title: Bank of Italy: stablecoins show no consistent cost edge for remittances
stories.summary: A Bank of Italy study found that stablecoins do not offer a consistent cost advantage over traditional methods for cross-border remittances, challenging one of the frequently cited use cases for stablecoin adoption.
stories.whyItMatters: Remittances are often touted as a killer use case for stablecoins; a central bank finding undercutting that claim could temper policy and industry narratives around stablecoin utility.
whatToWatch: Responses from stablecoin issuers or remittance firms to the findings
Whether other central banks publish similar comparative studies
questions: Did the study account for variation across corridors and providers, or is it a broad average?

stories.title: US sanctions Iran-linked bitcoin insurance scheme for Strait of Hormuz shipping
stories.summary: The US has sanctioned companies involved in an Iran-linked scheme that reportedly used bitcoin to provide insurance for ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, part of a broader effort to close off sanctions-evasion channels tied to Iranian oil shipping.
stories.whyItMatters: The case shows crypto being used to route around traditional sanctions infrastructure, reinforcing why regulators continue to focus enforcement attention on crypto's role in illicit finance.
whatToWatch: Additional sanctions actions targeting related entities or wallets
Any crypto industry response on compliance and monitoring implications
questions: How significant was the scale of bitcoin used in this insurance scheme?
Will this prompt tighter scrutiny of crypto used in shipping-related finance more broadly?
